programme: BRD4 (BET bromodomain reader) opens H3K27ac-marked chromatin at ATF3, and ATF3 in turn represses the cystine transporter SLC7A11; in parallel KLF6 drives NSUN2-dependent m5C modification of NCOA4 to trigger ferritinophagy. Together BRD4, ATF3 and KLF6 form an epigenetic-to-transcriptional cascade that licenses ferroptotic/regulated cell death.
role_in_a: In Sjögren's syndrome, only BRD4 has direct evidence: an ML-based transcriptomic study flags it as a pyroptosis-pathway biomarker/target in primary Sjögren's (PMID 41410587) — a related but distinct regulated-cell-death programme to the ferroptosis mechanism documented for this module in stroke. ATF3 carries only a moderate Open Targets score in Sjögren's and no supporting paper; KLF6 has no recorded association or paper in Sjögren's at all.
role_in_b: In stroke the same three factors form a described cascade: BRD4 silencing blunts hemin-induced neuronal ferroptosis via the H3K27ac-ATF3 axis (PMID 40605044); ATF3 promotes ferroptosis by repressing SLC7A11 (PMID 41314556), is dually regulated with Lonp1 in cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury (PMID 40044488), and has been proposed as a serum severity marker (PMID 41250979); KLF6 activates NSUN2-mediated m5C modification of NCOA4 to enhance ferroptosis in OGD/R models, and its silencing attenuates MCAO-induced brain injury via the same pathway (PMID 41478321, PMID 39710598).
shared_axis: BRD4 behaves as a general epigenetic licensor of stress-induced regulated cell death rather than a pathway-specific factor, so the same reader could drive pyroptotic gene programmes in Sjögren's-affected glandular/immune tissue while driving the ATF3/KLF6 ferroptotic cascade in ischaemic neurons — different death modality, same upstream chromatin logic. This is a mechanistic hypothesis, not a documented fact: no source here states the two diseases share this axis.
reasoning: The module is nameable and mechanistically coherent (BRD4→ATF3 is a stated regulatory relationship in one paper, and KLF6 converges on the same ferroptosis endpoint independently), and the stroke arm is strongly and repeatedly documented across all three factors. But the Sjögren's arm rests on a single biomarker paper for BRD4 alone, in a different death pathway (pyroptosis, not ferroptosis), so the cross-disease link is inferred, not retrieved.
support: PMID 40605044 — BRD4 silencing attenuates hemin-induced neuronal ferroptosis via H3K27ac-ATF3 axis (stroke, establishes BRD4→ATF3 link); PMID 41314556 — ATF3 promotes ferroptosis by repressing SLC7A11 in ischemic stroke; PMID 40044488 — ATF3/Lonp1 dual regulation as therapeutic targets in cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion; PMID 41250979 — ATF3 as a serological severity marker in stroke; PMID 41478321 — KLF6 activates NSUN2/NCOA4 m5C-driven ferroptosis in OGD/R; PMID 39710598 — KLF6 silencing attenuates MCAO-induced brain injury via ferroptosis; PMID 41410587 — BRD4 as a pyroptosis-pathway biomarker/target in primary Sjögren's syndrome (different death modality, disease A only).
how_to_falsify: Measure ferroptosis markers (SLC7A11 repression, NCOA4/NSUN2-dependent ferritinophagy, labile iron/lipid peroxidation) in Sjögren's-affected salivary/lacrimal gland tissue or PBMCs, and test whether BET inhibition (e.g. JQ1) or BRD4 knockdown shifts these markers the way it does in the stroke models cited above. If Sjögren's tissue shows no ferroptosis signature and no BRD4-ATF3 coupling despite BRD4 dysregulation, the shared-axis account is wrong and BRD4's roles in the two diseases are independent.
caveats: Tissue pairing is recorded as blood|blood, but nearly all mechanistic support for this module comes from neuronal/cerebral injury models (OGD/R, MCAO, hemin-induced ICH), not blood or PBMC data — a translation gap the account cannot close with what's here. 21 patient-group comparisons drawn from only 4 independent cohort pairs is modest replication, and the carrying factors sit at 12-14/21, not near-universal. Several other concordant factors (BCL3, DBP, TCF7L2, E2F4, POU2F2, TFEC, SP2, FOXL1, ELK4) were deliberately left out because no retrieved evidence ties them into this specific epigenetic/ferroptosis cascade — they recur but do not cohere with it. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed the obvious immune master-regulator candidates for a blood-tissue autoimmune/vascular pair (CIITA, IRF1, FOXO3/FOXO4, LEF1, RUNX2, SMAD3, FLI1, E2F1, ID3, LITAF), which is why this account had to reach for a less obvious module rather than a generic inflammation story.
